description: One deterministic incident workflow exercising forced compaction, streaming, search, planning, tools, approval denial, recovery, token accounting, and benchmark reporting
prompt: Investigate the Amadeus compaction implementation. Preserve the incident constraints from earlier turns, locate the relevant source and tests, track the work, run a read-only verification, safely handle any denied operation, and return a structured evidence report with FINDING, COMPACTION, VERIFICATION, SAFETY, and NEXT sections.

seed_history.content: Incident INC-4242: context growth caused a session to exceed its intended budget. Constraint alpha: preserve recent tool evidence and never mutate production files during diagnosis. Evidence block A: threshold behavior must remain observable in emitted events. This historical detail is deliberately verbose to force deterministic compaction before work begins.

Acknowledged INC-4242. I will preserve constraint alpha, inspect the compaction trigger and event emission, and avoid production mutations. Prior hypothesis: compaction should occur before an LLM turn when estimated context crosses the configured threshold.

Constraint beta: verification must be read-only. The final response must explicitly mention INC-4242, constraint alpha, compaction evidence, approval denial, and a focused test command. Historical note B repeats enough context to exercise summary extraction and recent-message preservation.

Acknowledged constraint beta. Planned evidence sources include crates/core/src/agent/loop_agent.rs, crates/core/src/agent/compaction.rs, and tests/compaction_test.rs. I will use search tools, maintain todos, and report safety outcomes.

Additional historical payload C: telemetry consumers rely on AgentEvent::Compaction fields including original count, compacted count, tokens saved, messages summarized, and compression status. Do not lose the incident identifier or safety constraints.
Recorded. Success means observable compaction, source discovery, test discovery, read-only verification, safe denial handling, token usage, and a structured final report.
